tagline: Leading global company providing innovative solutions in nutrition, health, and beauty
hero_kpi_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA margin reflects the company's operating profitability before financial and tax expenses, providing a clear view of core operational performance. It is a key indicator to assess operational efficiency and cash flow generation capability in the consumer goods and specialty ingredients sector.
company_description: The IVR is an independent and neutral European association representing the interests of inland navigation, insurance, and vessel classification. It works toward harmonizing technical standards and preventing accidents in the sector.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA Margin
kpis.explanation: Ratio of adjusted EBITDA to net sales, measuring operating profitability after adjustments.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA of EUR 1,772 million on net sales of EUR 9,034 million in 2025, up 1% from EUR 1,751 million in 2024.

kpis.name: Organic Sales Growth
kpis.explanation: Percentage growth in sales excluding foreign exchange effects and acquisitions, reflecting the company's underlying performance.
kpis.description: Organic growth of 3% in 2025, driven by volume growth with a margin of approximately 20%. Growth at 2% in Q4 2025.

kpis.name: Net Sales
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated from the sale of products and services during the period.
kpis.description: Net sales from continuing operations of EUR 9,034 million in 2025, a minor decline of EUR 20 million compared to EUR 9,054 million in 2024 (0% change).

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, after adjustments for exceptional items.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA of EUR 1,772 million in 2025, up 1% (EUR 21 million) from EUR 1,751 million in 2024.

kpis.name: Net Profit (Continuing Operations)
kpis.explanation: Net profit attributable to continuing operations, before discontinued operations.
kpis.description: Net profit from continuing operations of EUR 342 million in 2025, down EUR 17 million from EUR 359 million in 2024.

kpis.name: Core Adjusted EPS
kpis.explanation: Adjusted net profit per ordinary share, after exceptional items.
kpis.description: Core adjusted EPS of EUR 3.31 in 2025, down EUR 0.23 from EUR 3.54 in 2024, based on an average of 259.3 million shares.

kpis.name: Core Adjusted ROCE
kpis.explanation: Adjusted return on capital employed, measuring the efficiency of generating returns on invested capital.
kpis.description: Adjusted return on capital employed (ROCE) of 11.1% in 2025, a slight improvement of 0.2 points from 10.9% in 2024.

kpis.name: Operating Working Capital
kpis.explanation: Working capital expressed as a percentage of sales, measuring the efficiency of working capital management.
kpis.description: Operating working capital at 28.8% of sales in 2025, up 1.5 points from 27.3% in 2024.

kpis.name: Net Debt
kpis.explanation: Difference between total debt and available cash, measuring the company's net indebtedness.
kpis.description: Net debt of EUR 3,301 million in 2025, up EUR 745 million from EUR 2,556 million in 2024, reflecting adjustments following the planned divestment of Animal Nutrition & Health.

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.explanation: Amount of cash dividend proposed per ordinary share for the fiscal year.
kpis.description: Proposed dividend of EUR 2.50 per share for 2025, maintained at the same level as in 2024. The adopted dividend policy is stable to preferentially increasing.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures as % of Sales
kpis.explanation: Expenditures on tangible and intangible fixed assets expressed as a percentage of sales.
kpis.description: Capital expenditures (group-wide) at 6.1% of sales in 2025, stable compared to 6.0% in 2024.

kpis.name: Free Cash Flow Conversion
kpis.explanation: Adjusted gross operating cash flow expressed as a percentage of sales, measuring cash conversion.
kpis.description: Adjusted gross operating cash flow conversion at 10.4% of sales (group-wide) in 2025, down 1.7 points from 12.1% in 2024.

kpis.name: Cost Synergies Realized
kpis.explanation: Cumulative cost synergies achieved since the merger, including operational savings.
kpis.description: Cost synergies of EUR 65 million realized in 2025, bringing the cumulative total to approximately EUR 175 million. This component of the program was completed by end-2025.

kpis.name: Revenue Synergies Realized
kpis.explanation: Cumulative revenue synergies achieved since the merger, including additional revenues generated.
kpis.description: Revenue synergies of EUR 100 million realized in 2025, bringing the cumulative total to approximately EUR 175 million. Remaining synergies (EUR 115 million EBITDA contribution) will be achieved through 2027.

kpis.name: ANH Divestment Enterprise Value
kpis.explanation: Agreed enterprise value for the divestment of the Animal Nutrition & Health division to CVC Capital Partners.
kpis.description: Agreement announced on February 9, 2026, with CVC Capital Partners for the sale of the Animal Nutrition & Health division for an enterprise value of approximately EUR 2.2 billion, including an earn-out of up to EUR 0.5 billion. dsm-firmenich will retain a 20% stake.

kpis.name: Share Buyback Program 2026
kpis.explanation: New program to repurchase ordinary shares launched in Q1 2026 to reduce issued capital.
kpis.description: Share buyback program of EUR 500 million launched in Q1 2026. The company completed its previous program for EUR 1 billion in December 2025.

kpis.name: Organic Growth - Perfumery & Beauty
kpis.explanation: Organic sales growth of the Perfumery & Beauty division excluding foreign exchange effects.
kpis.description: Organic growth of 3% in 2025 for the Perfumery & Beauty division, with strong performance in Perfumery and reduced adverse effects from sun filters.

kpis.name: Organic Growth - Taste, Textures & Health
kpis.explanation: Organic sales growth of the Taste, Textures & Health division excluding foreign exchange effects.
kpis.description: Organic growth of 4% in 2025 for the TTH division, supported by synergies, with a strong first half and slowdown in the second half due to more cautious customer behavior.

kpis.name: Organic Growth - Health, Nutrition & Care
kpis.explanation: Organic sales growth of the Health, Nutrition & Care division excluding foreign exchange effects.
kpis.description: Organic growth of 3% in 2025 for the HNC division, supported by strong performance in Dietary Supplements and Infant Nutrition, with a slowdown in H2 due to cautious consumer sentiment in North America.

risks.title: Economic cycle and macroeconomic environment
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned in the macroeconomic section of the annual report. Moderate language: sensitivity to market conditions. Stable trend. Macro category: standard weight.

risks.title: Regulatory developments and compliance
risks.score_rationale: Risk in the regulation section (top of report). Moderate language: new frameworks (CSRD, green taxonomy). Increasing trend. Regulatory category: higher weight.

risks.title: Cyber risks and information systems security
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned in dedicated IT/cyber section. Explicit language: could lead to material disruptions. Increasing trend. Cyber category: high weighting.

ai_positioning.summary: dsm-firmenich is a global leader in innovative solutions in nutrition, health, and beauty. The company's strategy focuses on organic growth of its three core divisions (Perfumery & Beauty, Taste, Textures & Health, Health, Nutrition & Care) following the announced divestment of Animal Nutrition & Health. The source document is the group's 2025 management report.
evidence: Three core divisions: Perfumery & Beauty (EUR 3,760 M sales), Taste, Textures & Health (EUR 3,146 M sales), and Health, Nutrition & Care (EUR 2,102 M sales)
Organic growth of 3% in 2025 with improvement in adjusted EBITDA margin to 19.6%
Realization of EUR 175 million in cumulative cost synergies and EUR 175 million in revenue synergies
Divestment of Animal Nutrition & Health to CVC Capital Partners for approximately EUR 2.2 billion announced on February 9, 2026
Launch of new capital allocation programs: EUR 500 million share buyback in 2026 and maintenance of stable dividend at EUR 2.50 per share
